question: Which of the following rulers started the practice of measuring land during the Mughal period?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Akbar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Akbar, the third Mughal emperor, introduced several important administrative reforms during his reign.
 
• One of his **major reforms **was the introduction of a systematic method for **measuring land for revenue purposes**.
 
• This system, known as the "**Zabt**" system, was introduced in the 16th century and became a cornerstone of Mughal revenue administration.
 
• Under this system, **land was measured and categorized for the purpose of assessing and collecting land revenue**.
 
• This practice allowed for a more standardized and fair collection of taxes, contributing to the stability and prosperity of the Mughal Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shershah Suri**

 
 
• Before Akbar, Shershah Suri also introduced several administrative reforms, including the construction of roads and the introduction of a new currency.
 
• However, he did not establish a systematic method for measuring land as Akbar did.
 
 
 
• **Shahjahan**
 
 
• Shahjahan, another Mughal emperor, is best known for his architectural achievements, including the construction of the Taj Mahal.
 
• He continued the administrative practices established by his predecessors but did not introduce any significant new land measurement systems.
 
 
 
• **Aurangzeb**
 
 
• Aurangzeb was the last of the great Mughal emperors and is known for his expansionist policies and strict adherence to Islamic law.
 
• He also continued the administrative systems established by Akbar but did not introduce any new methods for measuring land.
